saints.name: St. Lidwina of Schiedam
saints.title: Virgin
saints.shortBlurb: A Dutch maiden whose thirty-eight years of illness became a school of redemptive suffering…
biography: Lidwina was born at Schiedam in Holland in 1380. At about fifteen she fell while ice-skating and broke a rib; the injury never healed, and she passed the rest of her life bedridden, her body wracked by an illness that grew ever more grievous over some thirty-eight years.

Rather than despair, Lidwina offered her sufferings for sinners and for the Church, was granted visions and a deep union with the Passion, and in her later years is said to have taken almost no food but the Eucharist. Widely revered in her own lifetime, she died in 1433; her cult was confirmed by Pope Leo XIII in 1890, and she is invoked as a patron of the chronically ill.
saints.knownFor: Bearing long illness as an offering of redemptive suffering.

canonization.canonized: Cult confirmed 1890 by Pope Leo XIII

sources.text: Butler, Lives of the Saints (1866 ed.), 14 April
